hints.title: Cyclic Match Condition
hints.text: A character c1 matches c2 if c1 == c2 or the cyclic successor of c1 equals c2 (with z wrapping to a).

hints.title: Greedy Matching
hints.text: Use two pointers i and j. Advance through str1 and match characters of str2 greedily as early as possible.

hints.title: Subsequence Completion
hints.text: If j reaches the end of str2, then str2 can successfully be formed as a subsequence.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def canMakeSubsequence(self, str1: str, str2: str) -> bool:
        i, j = 0, 0
        n, m = len(str1), len(str2)
        while i < n and j < m:
            c1 = str1[i]
            c2 = str2[j]
            nxt = chr((ord(c1) - ord('a') + 1) % 26 + ord('a'))
            if c1 == c2 or nxt == c2:
                j += 1
            i += 1
        return j == m
```

complexity.notes: Single pass greedy two-pointer subsequence matching with cyclic check.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Examining all subsets or substrings of str1 leads to exponential time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Apply greedy two-pointer matching with modulo arithmetic for cyclic character transitions.
